main_text.p: δεῖνι μεμφόμενος, ἢ τὸν δεῖνα ἀπάξιον εἶ) φά- σκων, cuidam detrahens, & quendam indignum esse dicens.

Contrá, sæpe nomen est sine articulo: Socrat. apud Stobæum, πατρὸς ὑβριμάνοις, ἡδὺ φαρμακον, patris objurgatio, dulce medicamentū. Sophocl. ἐχθρῶν ἀδῶρα δῶρα, hostium dona non sunt dona. Eurip. φύλλα γὰρ οἴκων εἰσὶ παῖ- δες ἀρόσενες, columnæ enim familiarum, sunt filii mares.
In his omnibus exemplis, articulus omittitur. Sed Homericus locus ille, exempli plenioris est, lib. Il.ς, & θ: .
main_text.l: ἔνθα δ᾽ ἀμ᾽ οἰμωγή τε ἡ δ᾽ ἀλωλὴ πόλεν ἀνδρῶν
ὀλλύντων ἡ ὀλλυμένων· ῥέε δ᾽ αἵματι γαῖα.

p.i: Tum vero simul ejulatusq; & exultatio erat virorum
Perdentium & pereuntium: fluebat autem sanguine terra.

page.notes: Greek text in the first lines is partly blurred; some accents and breathings are uncertain and were transcribed as best read. The Homeric passage is printed with the Greek line for "ἔνθα" slightly displaced; readings of the Greek are approximate.
